topic: Past customers are the warmest list you own and the one you never contact.

slides.subtitle: (and have not heard from you since)
slides.scene: A row of old paper job dockets on a spike file on a workshop shelf, curled and faded with age, every docket completely blank, dust visible along the top edge. All vehicles and buildings in shot have COMPLETELY BLANK panels and surfaces with absolutely no writing, no company name, no logo, no lettering, no phone number and no graphics of any kind. No signage anywhere in the scene. There is NO text, no words and no labels anywhere in the image.

caption:
Somebody you did good work for two winters ago is currently searching for your trade.

Not because they were unhappy. Because it has been two years, the furnace is making the noise again, and your name is not the one that came to mind.

That is the whole loss. Not a bad review, not a complaint. Just time passing quietly while nobody said anything.

Every contractor has this list. It is sitting in the invoicing software and it is the warmest list you will ever own, because every name on it has already paid you once and did not regret it.

A note before the season turns is enough. Not a campaign. A reminder that you exist, sent at a moment when the thought is useful rather than annoying.

The reason it never happens is that it has to happen in August, and in August you are flat out.

Comment DISPATCH and I will send the plan.
